name: Prone press-up
movement: lying face down, the chest pressed up on the hands with the hips kept on the floor, and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: Lying face down, the chest pressed up on the hands while the hips stay on the floor.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie face down side on to it, hands under the shoulders, legs relaxed.
words.position: Lie face down, side on to the phone, hands flat under the shoulders, legs and hips relaxed on the floor.
words.top: The chest pressed up on the hands, the back curved and the hips still on the floor — only as far as is comfortable — held a moment and lowered.
howto: Lie face down, hands flat under the shoulders, legs relaxed. Let the back and hips go loose.
Press the hands into the floor and push the chest up, letting the back sag between the hips and the shoulders. The arms do the work; the back muscles stay relaxed.
Keep the hips on the floor. Go only as far as is comfortable, and hold a moment.
Lower slowly. The rep counts when the chest is back on the floor.
words.cannot: Whether the back muscles are relaxed and where the pain is moving: it sees the chest rising and the hips lifting. Let the arms do all of it.
words.about: Prone press-up — face down side on: the press, as the hip-to-shoulder line off level, at least 20° at the top (flat reads near 0; on the elbows about 30; a full press with straight arms about 45) — only as far as is comfortable; a rep is under way past 15 and counts when the chest is back under 8; and the hips on the floor, the knee-to-hip line no more than 5° above where it started — the hips coming up turns it into a push-up; and the legs relaxed on the floor, the knees not lifting more than 8° — that is the back muscles doing it. Hold two seconds at the top. A McKenzie extension: ten reps, repeated through the day, with the range growing as it eases; pain that moves toward the spine is the sign to keep going, pain that moves down the leg the sign to stop.
words.lost: Lie face down side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the pain spreads further down the leg. The back muscles stay relaxed; the arms press.
words.easier: Up onto the elbows rather than the hands; a smaller press; a shorter hold.
words.harder: Straight arms; a longer hold; a breath out at the top to let the hips sink.
words.mistakes: Lifting the hips off the floor; lifting the legs or tensing the back to lift; holding the breath; pushing into sharp pain.

measurements.label: chest raised
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off level: flat near 0, pressed up on straight arms about 45. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Chest raised at the top, at least (degrees)

measurements.label: hip above the knee
measurements.why: The knee-to-hip line off level, as its change since the start: + the hips coming up with the press, which is a push-up, not an extension; − the knees lifting off the floor, the back muscles doing the work. Read against the start, since the shape of the body alone tilts it a few degrees.

faults.text: Press up a little higher — only as far as is comfortable

faults.text: Keep the hips on the floor — let the back sag
faults.deep: The hips are up — this is a push-up; lower them and press less
